title: Models
coreMove: Use models as lenses, not badges: choose the one that clarifies cause, communication, change, or team behavior, then let it alter the next decision.

exampleSpecs.domain: software recovery review after a failed pilot
exampleSpecs.audience: project leaders choosing a response to uncertain work
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may name complexity while still forcing linear planning logic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the scene opens after failure and locates the one misstep left on the wall

exampleSpecs.stakes: early friction may be punished as failure instead of shaped into norms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist notices her own wrong reading mid-stream

exampleSpecs.domain: maintenance notice that keeps being misread
exampleSpecs.stakes: a sent message may be mistaken for shared understanding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a written artifact carries the action through sender, receiver, noise, and feedback

exampleSpecs.domain: two product teams entering early conflict
exampleSpecs.audience: managers choosing how to respond to team friction
exampleSpecs.stakes: one team may mature while another suppresses the conflict it needs to work through
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people face the same situation with opposite approaches and divergent outcomes

exampleSpecs.domain: delivery lead stuck in complexity language
exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who can name uncertainty but still plan it incorrectly
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may use the right model without changing the response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a peer reframes the stuck view in one quotable sentence

exampleSpecs.audience: learners practicing model selection without workplace stakes
exampleSpecs.stakes: the learner may memorize model names without knowing what question each one answers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the learner's confusion becomes the material of the lesson
